subject: Extracting methbase or methDiff rows based on a gRanges file

messages.author: b5b1db21b60ddd4a
messages.subject: Extracting methbase or methDiff rows based on a gRanges file
parts:
HI,

 

I thought I saw a post on this, but I searched and cannot find it.

 

I want to extract from either my methbase or methdiff file all the lines of data that correspond (or overlap with) lines of regions I have in a gRanges file.

 

I have seen the function:

extract-methods

where the examples are essentially extracting a certain number of lines of data:

 

# selects first hundred rows, returns a methylBase object

subset2=methylBase.obj[1:100,]

 

I have tried and failed with:

p2=meth2[(d$IRanges),]

p2=meth2[(d$ranges),]

 

 

I want to do the same with a gRanges file “d” and extract my CG data in a strand specific manner.

I have also tried findOverlaps with no luck.

p2<-findOverlaps(as(meth2,"GRanges"),d$IRanges)

Error in (function (classes, fdef, mtable)  :

  unable to find an inherited method for function ‘findOverlaps’ for signature ‘"GRanges", "NULL"’

 

It seems like a simple thing but for some reason I am struggling?

So how can I extract the data with the right ranges on the correct strand?

 

Thanks,

 

Michelle

messages.author: e4181d5c40fc094c
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Extracting methbase or methDiff rows based on a gRanges file
parts:
I am trying to repeat your question! Let me know if I got it right or not!
  • You have
    •  GRanges object 'd'
    • methylBase object (meth2)
  • You want to extract the ranges from meth2 that are either common or overlap 'd' or vice versa

In such a case I would do the following:

#Convert meth2 to GRanges

meth_ranges=as(meth2,"GRanges")

# Find intersection (in case common ranges are needed)

common=intersect(meth_ranges,d)

# Find overlaps (in case of overlaps that includes subset of ranges). Makes sure if you want to identify overlapping ranges from meth_ranges or d. One of the following will suit

overlaps_in meth_ranges=subsetByOverlaps(meth_ranges,d)

overlaps_in_d=subsetByOverlaps(d,meth_ranges)

Let us know if you got the answer!
